# Lee – going halves on a dumper

Rather than keep bending your ear about it in the van, here are the sums.

**What hiring is costing us**

We’ve hired the tracked dumper for 14 days this year from the place in Sittingbourne. At £85 a day, plus £30 delivery each time, that’s roughly **£1,600 all in**.

It’s not just the money either. In September they didn’t have one available, so we ended up barrowing six ton of muck at the Hernhill job. That added two extra days and your back was gone for a week. Another time the delivery driver didn’t turn up until 11, so we lost half the morning waiting around.

**The one for sale**

There’s a bloke in Faversham selling a **2019 500kg tracked dumper for £1,650 ono**. He says it had new tracks fitted last spring. I can check all that over when I see it.

Going halves at the full asking price would be **£825 each**, hopefully less if we can knock him down. It can live in my lean-to at the yard, so it’ll be covered and storage is sorted.

At this year’s level of use, it would pay for itself in about a year. Even if we only used it half as much, I’re looking at roughly two years. That’s before servicing and any repairs, so I’m not pretending there’s no cost or risk after buying it.

But we’ve already got **three patio digs and the Boughton drive booked in for spring**, so it’s not as though it would sit there doing nothing. If it doesn’t work out, we can sell it on and split what we get back. These things hold their value pretty well.

**How I’d split it**

- Purchase price: 50/50  
- Servicing and general upkeep: 50/50  
- If one of us breaks it, that person pays for the repair  
- If we sell it: whatever we get back is split 50/50  

We’ve known each other 15 years, so you can be straight with me if you think it’s a bad idea. I just reckon it’s worth a proper look.

**Come to Faversham with me this Saturday and give it a once-over.** If it’s rough, we walk away, but I’d rather see it before someone else has it.
